readings.title: Hapgood’s stated scope
readings.text: I have used the Old Church-Slavonic books of the Russian Church, rather than the original Greek, because my work has been done, prima- rily, for the use of the Russian Church in America. Slight differences in arrangement and practice (not in dogma) have arisen between the Russian Church and the Greek Church, similar to those between the Church of England and the Protestant Episcopal Church in America. I have carefully compared everything with the original Greek.

readings.title: Published books and custom
readings.text: It will be seen that I have been confronted with the problem of re- jection, as well as of judicious selection. I may add, that many things are done or said "by custom " which are not mentioned in the printed books. These I have included.

readings.title: For whom did Hapgood prepare her service book?

paragraphs.text: Hapgood says she worked primarily for the Russian Church in America and used its Church Slavonic books while comparing them with the Greek. She distinguishes differences of arrangement and practice from differences of dogma, meaning doctrine. This explains the particular background of the edition used throughout these lessons.
paragraphs.reason: The owner authorized a plain-English curriculum explanation so beginners can understand the topic before consulting the preserved source passage.

readings.title: Why can printed books and parish practice differ?

paragraphs.text: Hapgood states that some things said or done by custom are not recorded in the printed books. She therefore describes editorial selection as well as translation. The observation identifies the limits of using one published book as an exhaustive account of lived church practice.
